mutants.killTest: NotAuditedWhenSetupRecordAbsent: ResetChangeLogState(); ChangeLogSetup.DeleteAll(); ChangeLogMgt.InitChangeLog(); Assert.IsFalse(AuditCheck.WouldLogUserChanges(), 'Must return false when there is no Change Log Setup record'). Teardown ResetChangeLogState() re-inserts the row. Also discriminates a bare ChangeLogSetup.Get() with no not-found handling, which errors instead of returning false.

mutants.justification: Deletes CGX025DocLog.Init() inside the OnInsert trigger. CGX025DocLog is declared in that trigger's own var section, so it is a fresh per-invocation local, which AL already initialises blank at scope entry. Table 'CG X025 Doc Log' declares no InitValue on either field; 'Doc Entry No.' is assigned on the next line and 'Entry No.' is AutoIncrement. No OnInsert trigger on the log table, so Insert(true) observes nothing. Redundant Init() on a fresh, fully-overwritten local. M0001 and M0003 on the same trigger ARE killed.

Deletes CGX046Archive.Init() in procedure Archive. Fresh procedure local, never Get()/Find()-ed and never assigned before this point, so already blank at scope entry. Prereq table has three fields, none with InitValue, and all three plus SystemId are assigned before Insert(false, true). RunTrigger=false so no trigger observes pre-Insert state. NOT a wrong-fix variant of the planted trap: M0002, M0003 and M0005 - the Stash, the Get and the Insert - are all killed.

AddHeader stores Set(Value, Name), keying the dictionary by header VALUE; the oracle only asserts Result.Contains('Content-Type')/Contains('Authorization') and both tokens still appear as dictionary values, so the key-role inversion is invisible. Observable format-agnostically: two headers sharing one value collide into a single entry under the mutant.
mutants.killTest: TestAddHeader_DistinctNamesSharingOneValue: build with AddHeader('X-Trace-Id','shared-token') and AddHeader('X-Correlation-Id','shared-token'). Assert Contains('X-Trace-Id'), Contains('X-Correlation-Id'), Contains('shared-token'). Original keeps two entries; M0004 collapses them under 'shared-token' and loses X-Trace-Id. The third assert also kills M0013.

mutants.justification: Deleting AppendLine('Headers:') removes only a literal section label, not any header entry. The spec bounds Build to 'Build(): Text - returns formatted representation containing URL, method, headers, body, timeout', so the label string is a free formatting choice and no spec-derivable assertion distinguishes the two texts.

Dropping RequestHeaders.Get(HeaderName, HeaderValue) leaves HeaderValue blank every iteration, so ALL header values vanish from the built text while the names remain; the oracle asserts only header names. Header values are in scope: 'AddHeader(Name: Text; Value: Text) ... adds to RequestHeaders dictionary', plus Build must contain 'headers'.
mutants.killTest: Same test as M0004, third assertion Contains('shared-token'). Standalone variant: AddHeader('Content-Type','application/json') then Assert.IsTrue(Result.Contains('application/json')).

mutants.justification: The StrSubstNo swap emits the same two tokens per header, transposed around a delimiter the spec never fixes ('returns formatted representation containing URL, method, headers, body, timeout'). Any assertion detecting the transposition would impose an unspecified layout, and the dictionary itself is untouched.

Emptying Create's body removes all five Clear calls (and exit(Builder), inert because SingleInstance = true makes every returned instance share state), so Create returns an instance still carrying the previous request. Spec item 7 requires 'Create() ... returns a new cleared instance'; TestCreate_ReturnsNewInstance overwrites URL and method after Create and asserts only Contains('second.com').
mutants.killTest: TestCreate_DropsPreviousRequest kills M0018-M0023 together: build a stale request (URL https://stale.example/path, DELETE, header X-Stale-Header/stale-header-value, distinctive body, timeout 987654), then Fresh := Builder.Create(); Cleared := Fresh.Build(); six IsFalse asserts with NO setters in between, one per leaked field. M0018 fails all six.

mutants.killTest: TestCreate_DropsPreviousRequest: Assert.IsFalse(Cleared.Contains('https://stale.example/path'), 'New request should not report an address it was never given').

mutants.justification: Removing Clear(RequestMethod) leaks the previous method; masked by the oracle's immediate SetMethod('POST') after Create. Spec item 7 mandates a cleared instance.
mutants.killTest: TestCreate_DropsPreviousRequest: Assert.IsFalse(Cleared.Contains('DELETE'), 'New request should not report a method it was never given').

mutants.justification: Removing Clear(RequestHeaders) leaves every previously added header in the shared dictionary after Create; the oracle never re-inspects headers after Create. Spec item 7 mandates a cleared instance.
mutants.killTest: TestCreate_DropsPreviousRequest: IsFalse on both 'X-Stale-Header' and 'stale-header-value'.

mutants.justification: Removing Clear(RequestBody) leaks the previous body into the built text after Create; the oracle asserts nothing about the body after Create. Spec item 7 mandates a cleared instance.
mutants.killTest: TestCreate_DropsPreviousRequest: Assert.IsFalse(Cleared.Contains(the stale body text), 'New request should not report a body it was never given').

mutants.justification: Removing Clear(RequestTimeout) leaks the previous timeout; the oracle asserts nothing about the timeout after Create. Spec item 7 mandates a cleared instance.
mutants.killTest: TestCreate_DropsPreviousRequest: Assert.IsFalse(Cleared.Contains('987654'), ...). The distinctive 987654 avoids a false pass against the '0' a cleared Integer renders as.

mutants.justification: Line 9, two-argument overload: UnitPrice <= 0 errors on a zero price, but the spec bounds the raise to negative input ('Price must be positive for negative prices'), and the oracle already commits to that reading on the sibling parameter via TestCalculateLineTotalZeroQuantity. No test passes a zero unit price.
mutants.killTest: TestCalculateLineTotalZeroPrice: Assert.AreEqual(0, CalculateLineTotal(10, 0), 'A line priced at zero should total zero'). Original returns 0; M0003 raises the price error.

mutants.justification: Line 19, three-argument overload: Quantity <= 0 errors on zero quantity. Zero quantity is asserted only against the two-argument overload, so the discount overload's copy of the guard is never exercised at the boundary; the spec bounds the raise to negative quantities.
mutants.killTest: TestCalculateLineTotalZeroQuantityWithDiscount: Assert.AreEqual(0, CalculateLineTotal(0, 100.00, 10), 'A line of zero quantity should total zero even with a discount'). A companion assert kills M0007 in the same test.

mutants.justification: Line 21, three-argument overload: UnitPrice <= 0 errors on a zero price; no test calls the discount overload with a zero price, and the spec restricts the price error to negative prices.
mutants.killTest: Same test as M0006: Assert.AreEqual(0, CalculateLineTotal(10, 0, 10), 'A line priced at zero should total zero even with a discount').

mutants.justification: Turning the discount guard's or into and makes it unsatisfiable, so the only inputs whose behaviour changes are out-of-range discounts. The spec's error contract is exhaustive and names neither: 'Include proper error handling: CalculateLineTotal should raise Quantity must be positive for negative quantities and Price must be positive for negative prices'. Discount-range validation is the reference solution's own addition.

DiscountPercent <= 0 differs on exactly one input, DiscountPercent = 0, where it raises instead of returning Quantity * UnitPrice. A zero discount is an in-range value of the spec's own parameter, so its result is spec-determined; the oracle only ever passes discount 10.
mutants.killTest: TestCalculateLineTotalZeroDiscount: Assert.AreEqual(1000.00, CalculateLineTotal(10, 100.00, 0), 'A zero discount should leave the line total unreduced').

mutants.justification: DiscountPercent >= 100 differs only at DiscountPercent = 100, where it raises instead of returning 0. 100 is a legitimate value of the spec's DiscountPercent parameter and the top of the range the reference itself accepts; no test passes 100. Weaker spec support than M0009 (a full-discount line is the arguable edge), but the literal spec authorises no discount rejection at all.
mutants.killTest: TestCalculateLineTotalFullDiscount: Assert.AreEqual(0, CalculateLineTotal(10, 100.00, 100), 'A line discounted in full should total zero').

mutants.justification: RecRef is a procedure-local RecordRef and FieldCnt was captured on the preceding line, so removing RecRef.Close() before exit(FieldCnt) changes no return value and no caller-visible state; the runtime disposes the local record instance at procedure return and AL exposes no way for a test to observe the earlier release. The spec does say 'Always close the RecordRef', but there is no observation channel from a test body, unlike the removed Open calls M0008/M0015/M0023/M0024 which are killed by 'The record is not open'.

KeyIdx >= RecRef.KeyCount makes the highest VALID key index return empty text; the spec bounds the empty result to 'Return empty text if KeyIdx exceeds KeyCount', and KeyIdx = KeyCount does not exceed it. Every oracle test passes KeyIdx = 1, and this mutant surviving proves KeyCount >= 2 at runtime (declared PK plus the platform SystemId key).
mutants.killTest: TestGetNthKeyFieldName_HighestKeyIndex: RecRef.Open(69300); Expected := RecRef.KeyIndex(RecRef.KeyCount).FieldIndex(1).Name; assert non-empty, then Assert.AreEqual(Expected, GetNthKeyFieldName(69300, RecRef.KeyCount, 1)). Deriving Expected from the platform keeps it version-independent. Deterministic alternative: add a second declared key to prereq table 69300.

mutants.justification: Emptying the KeyIdx-out-of-range block deletes exit(''), so control falls through to RecRef.KeyIndex(KeyIdx) and errors with 'Index out of bounds' instead of returning empty text. The spec requires that branch; the oracle tests the out-of-range FieldIdx (which killed twin mutant M0020) but never an out-of-range KeyIdx.
mutants.killTest: TestGetNthKeyFieldName_KeyIndexOutOfRange: Assert.AreEqual('', GetNthKeyFieldName(69300, 99, 1), 'A key position the table does not have should report no field name'). Does NOT kill M0016, which still needs its own boundary test.

mutants.justification: Removing RecRef.Close() from the KeyIdx-out-of-range block still leaves exit(''), so the return value and all caller-visible state are unchanged and the local RecordRef is disposed at return regardless. Doubly unkillable: the block is currently unexecuted (proved by M0017 surviving), and even after adding the KeyIdx=99 kill test the Close removal stays unobservable from AL.

Same shape as M0018 in the FieldIdx-out-of-range block: exit('') still runs so the return value is identical; the block IS executed (TestGetNthKeyFieldName_OutOfRange killed sibling empty-block mutant M0020), confirming unobservability rather than mere non-coverage.

The success-path Close() at line 81 runs after FieldName := FldRef.Name has captured the result, so exit(FieldName) is unaffected and the local RecordRef dies at procedure return either way. Executed by TestGetNthKeyFieldName_First/_Third, so this is unobservability, not a coverage gap.

An empty body makes GetLockTimeoutPrevious return 0 without ever calling Database.LockTimeoutDuration, violating the spec's 'call Database.LockTimeoutDuration with the NewValue argument and return its Integer result'; the oracle's only assertion is the tautology Assert.IsTrue((Captured = Captured)), which holds for any return value, so the returned Integer is never checked at all.
mutants.killTest: LockTimeoutDurationValueIsReportedBack: call Demo.GetLockTimeoutPrevious(5000) once to prime, then Reported := Demo.GetLockTimeoutPrevious(5000) with the SAME value (under either reading of the platform semantics, returns-previous or returns-new-current, the second identical call must observe 5000), then Demo.GetLockTimeoutPrevious(10000) to restore the default, and assert Assert.AreEqual(5000, Reported, 'Expected the lock timeout duration just put in effect to be reported back'). Reported is 0 under M0001 and M0002. Also replace the existing tautological assert with this. If the platform normalizes the stored value, relax to Assert.AreNotEqual(0, Reported, ...), which still kills both.

mutants.justification: exit(0) drops both the call and the result, a real spec violation (the return must be the method's Integer result), and it survives because the oracle asserts only Captured = Captured.
mutants.killTest: Same test as M0001: the Assert.AreEqual(5000, Reported, ...) after two identical priming calls returns 0 under exit(0), so one test kills M0001 and M0002 together.

mutants.justification: The procedure takes no parameters and its only output is Refs.Count(), which is 2 whether or not the RecordRef was opened (List.Add accepts an unopened RecordRef - the mutant did not throw), and both RecordRefs are locals released at procedure return, leaving no state any caller can observe. No test written against the specified public surface (CountRecordRefList(): Integer) can distinguish it; the spec's Open requirement is enforced only by compile_pass, so closing this at runtime would require a task-spec change (exposing the refs), not an oracle change.

Identical to M0004 for the Item ref: the count returned is unaffected by whether the ref was opened, and the local ref dies at procedure return, so the difference is unobservable through the only public entry point.

An empty GetCallCount body returns 0 always, violating 'GetCallCount(): Integer - Returns current CallCount without incrementing'; all three covering tests use only relative or zero-valued asserts (AreEqual(CountBefore, CountAfter), AreEqual(0, CountAfterReset), AreEqual(Count1, Count2)), so a constant 0 satisfies every one of them and the nonzero count is never asserted anywhere in the oracle.
mutants.killTest: GetCallCountReportsTheNumberOfIncrements: Counter.Reset(); Counter.IncrementAndGet(); Counter.IncrementAndGet(); then Assert.AreEqual(2, Counter.GetCallCount(), 'Expected the call count to report the two increments already made'). Returns 0 under M0005 and M0006. Also harden the existing tests to absolutes: Assert.AreEqual(2, CountBefore, ...) / AreEqual(2, CountAfter, ...) in TestGetCallCountWithoutIncrement and Assert.AreEqual(2, Count2, ...) in TestSingleInstancePersistence, so a constant-0 getter cannot satisfy the SingleInstance test either.

mutants.justification: exit(0) in place of exit(CallCount) is the same real spec violation and survives for the same reason: no oracle assertion ever pins GetCallCount to a nonzero expected value.
mutants.killTest: Same test as M0005 - Assert.AreEqual(2, Counter.GetCallCount(), ...) after two increments fails at 0, killing M0005 and M0006 together.

mutants.justification: RecRef is a procedure-local RecordRef; the returned count is already captured in ResultCount before the removed Close(), and the local's handle is released by the runtime at the very next statement (exit(ResultCount)) whether or not Close() ran. RecordRef.Open takes no locks and writes nothing, so no caller, no later call, and no database state can distinguish the two forms - the spec's 'then close the RecordRef' is a code-shape requirement with no runtime observable at the AL surface.

Same structure in CountByDateRange: the count is computed into ResultCount before the removed Close(), and the local RecordRef is released at procedure return one statement later, so there is no reachable observation - no leak accumulates across calls because the handle dies with the local.

Without the category filter, CopyAToB iterates every row and copies non-A rows too, violating 'For every CG X004 Item whose Category is A, create one new ...'; it survives only because in all three tests every existing non-A row is itself a derived image (Entry No. = Tag + 1000), so Get(Tag + 1000) finds itself and the extra iterations are self-cancelling no-ops.
mutants.killTest: OnlyCategoryARowsAreCopied: Seed(2) (A rows tags 1..2), then insert a category-B row that is NOT a derived image - Item.'Entry No.' := 500; Item.Category := 'B'; Item.Tag := 7; Item.Insert(); Commit(); - then Assert.AreEqual(2, Copier.CopyAToB(), 'Expected only the two category-A items to produce new rows'), Assert.AreEqual(3, CountByCategory('B'), 'Expected the pre-existing category-B item plus one new row per category-A item'), and Assert.IsFalse(Item.Get(1007), 'Expected no row derived from a category-B item tag'). The mutant creates 1007 from tag 7, so it returns 3 and leaves 4 B rows - killed on all three asserts, and the result is independent of whether FindSet picks up rows inserted ahead of the cursor.

mutants.justification: 'CG X004 Item' has exactly three fields (Entry No., Category, Tag), no InitValue and no OnInsert trigger, and all three are assigned between the removed Init() and the Insert(); a stale record left in TargetItem by an earlier successful Get is therefore fully overwritten, and the run confirms Insert generates a fresh SystemId (the partial-overlap test does exactly Get-hit-then-Insert and did not error).

FlowFilter state set by SetRange persists on the Account record variable (Get ignores but does not clear filters, CalcFields does not clear them), so the identical SetRange already executed in the A block at line 17 is still in effect when the B block calls CalcFields - the removed line re-sets nothing (line 17's own mutant M0006 was correctly killed). The only input that separates the forms is a missing account A, which the YAML excludes: 'Three accounts, A, B, and C, already exist in the existing CG X051 Account table (ID 69111)'.

Same FlowFilter persistence for the C block: the filter is already in effect from the A (or B) block, so removing this SetRange changes nothing unless both A and B are absent, which the same YAML precondition ('Three accounts, A, B, and C, already exist') rules out; the exact fingerprint asserts (1797 / 2199) confirm the Normal-only balances are what the reference computes with the filter carried forward.

Drops the RecordId entry from _metadata, which task item 1 requires ('Include a _metadata object with TableName, TableId, and RecordId as string'); TestSerializeToJson_HasMetadata asserts only TableName and TableId.
mutants.killTest: TestSerializeToJson_MetadataIncludesRecordId: TestRecord.Code := 'RID001'; Insert; SerializeToJson; MetadataObj := token('_metadata').AsObject(); Assert.IsTrue(MetadataObj.Get('RecordId', JsonToken), 'Metadata should report the record identity'); Assert.AreEqual(Format(TestRecord.RecordId()), JsonToken.AsValue().AsText(), 'Reported record identity should match the record').

mutants.justification: Removes the Add in the Integer/BigInteger arm of AddFieldToJson, so whole-number fields vanish from the JSON; item 1 lists Integer among the types to handle, but every serialization test uses CG Test Record (Code/Text/Decimal/Boolean/Code) or asserts only No./Name on Customer, so no Integer field is ever asserted.

mutants.justification: Removes the Add in the Date arm, so Date fields vanish from the JSON; item 1 lists Date, but no serialization test uses a record with a Date field (CG Test Record has none, the Customer test asserts only No./Name).
mutants.killTest: TestSerializeToJson_ScalarFieldTypes (same test as M0010): RelatedRecord.'Created Date' := 20260115D; Assert.IsTrue(JsonResult.Get('Created Date', JsonToken)); Assert.AreEqual('2026-01-15', JsonToken.AsValue().AsText(), 'Created Date should match').

mutants.justification: Removes the Add in the DateTime arm; item 1 lists DateTime, and neither prereq table has a DateTime column so the arm is never asserted on any input the oracle constructs.
mutants.killTest: TestSerializeToJson_ScalarFieldTypes: requires a DateTime column - add field(7; 'Created At'; DateTime) to the CG-AL-H023 prereq table CG Related Record; set 'Created At' := CreateDateTime(20260115D, 120000T); assert Get('Created At') and AreEqual(Format(..., 0, 9), AsText()).

mutants.justification: Removes the Add in the Option arm, so Option/Enum fields vanish; item 1 lists Option and Enum, but neither prereq table has one and the Customer test asserts only No./Name.
mutants.killTest: TestSerializeToJson_OptionField: Customer.'No.' := 'CUST-OPT'; Customer.Blocked := Customer.Blocked::All; serialize; Assert.IsTrue(JsonResult.Get('Blocked', JsonToken)); Assert.AreEqual(3, JsonToken.AsValue().AsInteger(), 'Blocked should match the record').

mutants.justification: FieldsSet >= 0 makes DeserializeFromJson always report success once the table matches, violating item 2 ('Return true if at least one field was set, false if table mismatch or no fields set'); the two deserialize tests cover 4-fields-set (true) and table mismatch (false via the earlier exit) only.
mutants.killTest: TestDeserializeFromJson_NoMatchingFields: MetadataObj.Add('TableId', 69225); JsonData.Add('_metadata', MetadataObj); JsonData.Add('NotAField', 'x'); RecRef.Open(69225); Assert.IsFalse(DeserializeFromJson(JsonData, RecRef), 'Should report failure when no field values were applied').

mutants.justification: Turning the non-value guard into exit(true) counts an unassignable token as a field set, so DeserializeFromJson reports success while writing nothing - contrary to item 2's 'false if ... no fields set'; the oracle only ever supplies scalar values under field keys (the nested object it builds sits under _metadata, which is skipped).
mutants.killTest: TestDeserializeFromJson_NestedValueNotApplied: put an InnerObj under key 'Description'; Assert.IsFalse(Success, 'Should report failure when no field values were applied'); Assert.AreEqual('', GetFieldValueAsText(RecRef, 2), 'Description should stay blank').

mutants.justification: Turning the JSON-null guard into exit(true) counts a null as a field set, so the procedure reports success with nothing written, contrary to item 2's return contract; no test ever passes a null under a field key.
mutants.killTest: TestDeserializeFromJson_NullValueNotApplied: NullValue.SetValueToNull(); JsonData.Add('Description', NullValue); Assert.IsFalse(Success, ...); Assert.AreEqual('', GetFieldValueAsText(RecRef, 2), 'Description should stay blank').

mutants.justification: With 'and' the guard only fires when BOTH arguments are non-records, so a single non-record argument falls through to GetTable and errors instead of returning empty; item 3 requires 'Verify both are records of same table (return empty if not)' and all three CompareRecords tests pass two records.
mutants.killTest: TestCompareRecords_NonRecordInput: Record1.Code := 'CMP003'; NotARecord := 'just text'; Differences := CompareRecords(Record1, NotARecord); Assert.AreEqual(0, Differences.Count, 'Should be empty when a value that is not a record is supplied').

mutants.justification: Changing 'and' to 'or' makes non-Normal fields (FlowField/FlowFilter) pass the gate and get compared, violating item 3's 'Skip FlowFields and BLOB fields'; every field of CG Test Record is Normal and non-BLOB so both forms agree there, and the cross-table test exits before the loop.
mutants.killTest: TestCompareRecords_IgnoresCalculatedFields (needs one prereq line: field(6; 'Total Line Amount'; Decimal) FieldClass = FlowField, CalcFormula = sum('CG Related Record'.'Line Amount' where('Parent Code' = field(Code))) on CG Test Record). Insert parent + child, CalcFields on Rec1 only, then Assert.AreEqual(0, Differences.Count, 'Two reads of the same stored record should show no differences').

mutants.justification: exit(true) on a non-record source makes CloneRecord report success while copying nothing, contradicting item 4's 'Return true if successful'; both clone tests pass a real record.
mutants.killTest: TestCloneRecord_NonRecordSource: NotARecord := 'just text'; DestRecRef.Open(69225); Assert.IsFalse(CloneRecord(NotARecord, DestRecRef), 'Should report failure for a value that is not a record'); Assert.AreEqual('', GetFieldValueAsText(DestRecRef, 2), 'Destination should stay blank').

mutants.justification: exit(true) on a source/destination table mismatch reports a successful clone that never happened, contradicting item 4's 'Return true if successful'; both clone tests use CG Test Record on both sides. Note: item 4 has no explicit mismatch clause the way items 2 and 3 do - consider adding one to the YAML alongside this test.
mutants.killTest: TestCloneRecord_TableMismatch: SourceRecord.Code := 'MIS001'; DestRecRef.Open(18); Assert.IsFalse(CloneRecord(SourceRecord, DestRecRef), 'Should report failure when source and destination are different record types').

mutants.justification: 'or' lets non-Normal fields into the copy loop, so calculated fields are written to the destination, violating item 4's 'Copy all normal fields (not FlowFields, not BLOB)'; all CG Test Record fields are Normal so the two forms agree on the tables the oracle uses.
mutants.killTest: TestCloneRecord_LeavesCalculatedFieldsAlone (same prereq FlowField as M0037): CalcFields the source, clone, then Assert.AreEqual('0', GetFieldValueAsText(DestRecRef, 6), 'Calculated total on the destination should stay untouched').

mutants.justification: The original block contains only a comment, so both forms are an empty compound statement in the PK-preserving branch; no statement is added or removed.

Emptying GetDefaultValue makes it return '' for every type, so a numeric primary key at 0 is misread as already populated and CloneRecord keeps the destination's empty PK instead of copying the source's, breaking item 4's 'if DestRecRef already has PK set, keep it; otherwise copy from source'; for Code and Date PKs the correct default is also '' so the only tested table (CG Test Record, Code PK) cannot tell the two apart.
mutants.killTest: TestCloneRecord_CopiesNumericKeyWhenDestinationEmpty: Source.'Entry No.' := 4242; DestRecRef.Open(69228); clone; Assert.AreEqual('4242', GetFieldValueAsText(DestRecRef, 1), 'Key value should come from the source when the destination has none').

mutants.justification: Drops 'Length' from each schema element, which item 5 requires ('Each element is JsonObject with: FieldNo, FieldName, FieldType (as text), Length, FieldClass ... IsPartOfPrimaryKey'); TestGetTableSchema_ReturnsAllFields asserts Contains for every listed key except Length.
mutants.killTest: TestGetTableSchema_ReportsFieldLength: find FieldName = 'Description', FieldObj.Get('Length', JsonToken); Assert.AreEqual(100, JsonToken.AsValue().AsInteger(), 'Description length should match the table definition'); plus add Assert.IsTrue(FieldObj.Contains('Length')) to TestGetTableSchema_ReturnsAllFields.

mutants.justification: RecRef is a procedure-local RecordRef and the only statement after the removed Close() is exit(ResultArray); the returned JsonArray is already fully built and no caller can observe a local RecordRef's open state, which AL releases at scope exit.

exit(true) when more key values are supplied than the key has fields makes GetRecordByPrimaryKey report a find with an unfiltered, unpositioned RecordRef, contradicting item 7's 'Return true if record found, false otherwise'; both lookup tests pass exactly one value for the single-field key.
mutants.killTest: TestGetRecordByPrimaryKey_TooManyKeyValues: KeyValues.Add('FIND001'); KeyValues.Add('EXTRA'); Assert.IsFalse(GetRecordByPrimaryKey(69225, KeyValues, ResultRecRef), 'Should report not found when more key values are supplied than the key holds').

mutants.justification: Emptying the loop body applies no key filters, so FindFirst returns whatever row comes first in the table rather than the requested one; item 7 requires 'Filter by primary key fields using the provided KeyValues in order', and the oracle only ever has one row (or none) in CG Test Record when it looks up, so first-row and requested-row coincide.
mutants.killTest: TestGetRecordByPrimaryKey_SelectsTheRequestedRecord: insert Code 'AAA001'/Description 'First' and Code 'ZZZ999'/Description 'Last'; look up 'ZZZ999'; Assert.AreEqual('Last', GetFieldValueAsText(ResultRecRef, 2), 'Should return the requested record'); then assert a key that is not stored reports not found.

mutants.justification: Without KeyValues.Get the loop filters on an empty KeyVal, which is an empty (i.e. no) filter, so the lookup degenerates to first-row-in-table exactly as in M0085; it survived without erroring, proving the empty filter is accepted, and the oracle's one-row data cannot distinguish it.
mutants.killTest: TestGetRecordByPrimaryKey_SelectsTheRequestedRecord (same test as M0085) - the two-row setup makes first-row differ from requested-row.

mutants.justification: Removing SetFilter leaves the RecordRef unfiltered, so FindFirst returns the first row in the table instead of the requested key, against item 7's 'Filter by primary key fields using the provided KeyValues in order'; undetectable while the table holds at most the one row being looked up.
mutants.killTest: TestGetRecordByPrimaryKey_SelectsTheRequestedRecord (same test as M0085).

mutants.justification: Item 8 bounds TransformRecord as 'Apply transformations to each field: - Process all fields in the record' with no exclusion clause, unlike item 3 ('Skip FlowFields and BLOB fields') and item 4 ('Copy all normal fields (not FlowFields, not BLOB)'); the reference solution's Normal/non-BLOB gate is an unmandated implementation choice, so widening it to 'or' stays spec-compliant and the oracle must keep tolerating both (its TransformedCount asserts are deliberately open-ended).

The emptied block is the body of if SourceKeyRef.FieldCount() < 1, and KeyIndex(1) of any openable BC table always has at least one field, so the branch is unreachable for every input and its contents cannot affect behaviour.
This Close() sits inside the same SourceKeyRef.FieldCount() < 1 branch, which no real table can enter (every BC table's primary key has at least one field), so the statement is dead code.

Dropping Reset() lets the previous relating field's SetRange survive into the next iteration, so with two fields pointing at the source table the result becomes an intersection instead of per-field matches, against item 9's 'For each such field, filter by source record's primary key value'; CG Related Record has exactly one field relating to CG Test Record, so the loop body runs once on a fresh RecordRef and Reset is a no-op.
mutants.killTest: TestFindRelatedRecords_ChecksEachRelatingFieldIndependently (needs one prereq line: field(7; 'Alt Parent Code'; Code[20]) TableRelation = 'CG Test Record'.Code on CG Related Record). Insert one child via 'Parent Code' and one via 'Alt Parent Code', both pointing at 'MULTI1'; Assert.AreEqual(2, RelatedIds.Count, 'Both records referencing the parent should be reported').

mutants.justification: Removing SetRange returns every row of the related table regardless of which parent it points at, against item 9's 'filter by source record's primary key value'; the two FindRelatedRecords tests only ever have the intended children (or nothing) in CG Related Record, so unfiltered and filtered counts coincide.
mutants.killTest: TestFindRelatedRecords_IgnoresOtherParents: two parents, two children on PARENT1 and one on PARENT2; Assert.AreEqual(2, RelatedIds.Count, 'Only records referencing this parent should be reported').

Inverting IntVal = 0 to <> 0 makes ValidateRecordCompleteness report populated whole-number fields as missing and blank ones as present, against item 10's 'Integer/Decimal: 0 is invalid'; the three validation tests only pass Text, Decimal and Date field numbers, so the Integer/BigInteger/Option arm is never asserted.
mutants.killTest: TestValidateRecordCompleteness_IntegerField: 'Entry No.' := 4242, RequiredFields.Add(1), Assert.AreEqual(0, MissingFields.Count, 'A populated whole-number field should not be reported as missing'); then 'Entry No.' := 0 and Assert.IsTrue(MissingFields.Contains('Entry No.'), 'A zero whole-number field should be reported as missing').

The oracle never produces two cancellation entries, whereas M0030 - the byte-identical mutation on the release side - WAS killed by BatchReleasesValidOpenDocuments because that test does produce two release entries. mutants.killTest: New test ManualCancellationsOfSeveralDocumentsEachLeaveTheirOwnAlert: ResetAll(); SeedOpenDocument('D20', 500), ('D21', 500), ('D22', 500); call CancelAction.CancelWithAlert on D20, D21, D22 in turn; assert StatusOf each is 'Cancelled' and Assert.AreEqual(3, LogCountOf('CANCELLED'), 'Each manually cancelled document must leave its own cancellation activity entry'). Divergence needs OriginalWidth = MaxDimension with OriginalHeight <= MaxDimension, which forces the OriginalWidth >= OriginalHeight branch, where ThumbnailWidth := MaxDimension = OriginalWidth and ThumbnailHeight := Round(OriginalHeight * MaxDimension / OriginalWidth) = OriginalHeight exactly. The only differing input is a zero-length side (100x0 at maximum 100 gives 100x1 instead of 100x0), which is not an 'original picture's pixel width and height' and which the confirmed examples never cover, so no assertion should be added.

Mirror of M0003: divergence needs OriginalHeight = MaxDimension with OriginalWidth <= MaxDimension, and the scaling path then returns Round(OriginalWidth * MaxDimension / OriginalHeight) = OriginalWidth with ThumbnailHeight = MaxDimension = OriginalHeight, the identical box. Again only a zero-length side breaks the identity.

Divergence needs OriginalWidth = OriginalHeight past the already-fits guard, so both sides exceed MaxDimension; the taken branch yields (MaxDimension, Round(H*M/W)) = (M, M) and the swapped branch yields (Round(W*M/H), MaxDimension) = (M, M). A square original scales to a square either way for every MaxDimension >= 1.

The swap exchanges only the first two parameters, which appear in ScaleOtherSide solely as the product Side * MaxDimension; the divisor LongerSide is untouched, so the computed value is identical for every input by commutativity of integer multiplication.
Same commutativity argument as M0008 for the height-is-longer branch: Round(MaxDimension * OriginalWidth / OriginalHeight) equals Round(OriginalWidth * MaxDimension / OriginalHeight) for all inputs.

Scaled < 1 to Scaled <= 1 only adds the case Scaled = 1, and both arms then return 1 (the guard's exit(1) versus the fall-through exit(Scaled) with Scaled = 1), so the return value is unchanged for every input.

Policy is a procedure-local Record reached only after Policy.Get('') has already failed (so nothing was read into it), and the Refund Policy table has exactly two fields, 'Primary Key' and 'Approval Threshold', both assigned on the next two lines before Insert; Init() cannot change any field value.

Dropping Insert() leaves the policy table empty, so every call re-enters the branch and still returns 500; ApprovalThreshold()'s value is bit-identical for every call and no other code reads that table, leaving a row nothing consumes as the only difference. ApprovalThreshold is byte-identical to tasks/starter/CG-AL-X125/CGX125RefundReleaser.Codeunit.al and the task bounds the work to 'Fix the application so ReleaseRefund produces the confirmed behavior for every request it is given', never mentioning a policy record, so asserting the row's persistence would over-constrain a fix that legitimately restructures the threshold lookup.

Log is a procedure-local Record in LogDecline with no filter, mark, or key ever set on it before the Reset(), so Reset() has nothing to clear and the following FindLast() sees the same unfiltered primary-key ordering either way.

Init() sits after FindLast(), so removing it leaves the last-read row's values in the buffer, but the Decline Log table has exactly three fields (Entry No., Customer No., Amount) and all three are reassigned before Insert. ReleaseRefundHandlesManyRequestsAnsweredNo inserts 24 declines each preceded by a successful FindLast, exercising precisely this stale-buffer state and passing, which also confirms the platform regenerates SystemId on Insert.

Doc is a procedure-local record that AL blanks at scope entry and this is its first use, and all four fields of table 69930 (Batch Id, Line No., Status, Amount) are explicitly assigned on the next four lines before Insert(); the table declares no InitValue, so Init() cannot change any inserted value.

The only state ClearLastError() alters is the session last-error buffer, observable solely via GetLastErrorText/GetLastErrorCallStack; the DB path is provably unaffected (the mutant still satisfies the oracle's Doc.IsEmpty() open-residue assert). The YAML bounds the contract to 'reporting true when the Worker finished the batch and false when it did not, without letting a Worker failure interrupt PostDoc' plus row states on true/false, and says nothing about error text - a minimal correct submission would omit the call entirely, so requiring it would fail conforming fixes.

Doc is a fresh procedure-local on which PostDoc never sets a filter, mark, SetLoadFields or SetCurrentKey before line 23, and the Worker OnRun uses only its own locals (Marker/Line1/Line2) and never touches Rec, so nothing can come back through the var record of Codeunit.Run; Reset() therefore clears an empty filter set and re-selects the already-current primary key, and the two following SetRange calls fully determine the DeleteAll scope either way.

The only filter ever placed on Buffer is the SetRange(Label, ...) on the very next line, and AL SetRange on a field replaces any prior range on that same field, so the loop filter state after the SetRange is identical with or without Reset(); no SetCurrentKey, mark, or SetLoadFields is ever used, and neither IsEmpty() nor Insert() alters filters.

Table 69001 has exactly two fields and both (Entry No., Label) are assigned on the two lines immediately after the Init() and before Insert(), so the record is fully overwritten regardless of whether it still carries the previous iteration's inserted values; plain Insert() always generates a fresh SystemId, so the stale-SystemId route is closed too.

Both call sites (CountOpenSubItems:11, TotalEstimatedHours:28) declare ChildItem as their own local and call the local FindChildren exactly once on it - recursion allocates a new frame with a new record - so Reset() always runs on a scope-entry-fresh record with no filters, marks or non-default key to clear. Also byte-identical to tasks/starter/CG-AL-X111/CGX111WorkItemReport.Codeunit.al:53-59, i.e. starter code the fix does not touch.

Removing SetCurrentKey changes only the ORDER BY of the filtered FindSet/Next traversal, and FindChildren is local with exactly two consumers that aggregate order-insensitively - an integer count of open sub-items and an exact Decimal sum of Estimated Hours - so every returned value is identical; the SQL-statement budget test measures only OpenSubItemHoursAcrossChecklist, which never calls FindChildren. Also untouched starter code, per the same starter file.

The bare Get contributes only (a) an existence check already enforced by the platform on field 3's TableRelation = 'CG X118 Account'."No." - which is what still raises the error the oracle's SettingAnUnknownCounterAccountFailsWithAnError asserts under the mutant - and (b) the Currency Code feeding the reference's own defensive 'Rounding Precision' < 0 guard, a state the Currency table's MinValue = 0 makes unreachable through validation. The YAML bounds the fix to 'Amount and Balancing Amount always net to exactly zero once the counter account has been set'; the mutant (Balancing Amount := -Amount) is exactly the minimal conforming fix, so pinning the Get would fail correct submissions.

Flipping < 0 to <= 0 makes a counter currency whose Rounding Precision is exactly 0 - a value the Currency table explicitly permits (MinValue = 0) - raise 'invalid rounding precision' instead of balancing the line, contradicting the YAML's 'for any account and counter account, and whatever currency each side uses, a journal line Amount and Balancing Amount always net to exactly zero'. The oracle seeds only 0.01, 0.001 and 1 precisions, so the zero-precision boundary is never constructed.
mutants.killTest: Add AZeroPrecisionCounterCurrencyStillBalancesExactly: ClearAllData(); SeedCurrency('EUR', 0.01); SeedCurrency('ZPC', 0); SeedAccount('MAIN-EUR', 'EUR'); SeedAccount('CTR-ZPC', 'ZPC'); CreateLine(JournalLine, 17, 'MAIN-EUR'); SetAmountThenCounterAccount(JournalLine, 100.005, 'CTR-ZPC'); AssertBalances(17, 100.005). The mutant errors inside Validate('Counter Account No.') so the test fails before the asserts; the existing AssertBalances messages cover the value side. Bonus discriminating power: it also kills any submission keeping a Round(Amount, counterPrecision) shape, which divides by zero at this precision.

Spec bounds Fetch to 'retrieves the row identified by ItemNo into Item. It must bring back only the Description column'; SetLoadFields+Get alone satisfies that for every input, because Get ignores filters and re-reads the row, fully determining buffer contents and loaded-field set regardless of caller-supplied prior state. The only residual difference (caller filters/marks surviving, buffer on the not-found error path) is unconstrained by the spec, so the mutant is itself a spec-conformant solution the oracle must accept. Both load-bearing calls ARE pinned: removing SetLoadFields dies on FetchDoesNotBringBackTheOtherColumns, removing Get dies on FetchReturnsTheRequestedRow.

Result := Format(ValueRef.Value()) completes before RecRef.Close(), and RecRef/KeyRef/ValueRef are procedure locals never touched again, so the returned Text is identical either way. Each DescribeOf call opens its own fresh local RecordRef, so no state leaks across the oracle's five calls (two inside one test), and no lock or cursor an open RecordRef holds is observable in AL.

IsSameMoment is provably symmetric: the 0DT branch returns First = Second and the other returns Abs(First - Second) < 10, both symmetric, so IsSameMoment(a,b) = IsSameMoment(b,a) for every input pair and the swap at the ShouldResync call site cannot change any result. Stronger still: the spec demands symmetry ('whichever one is passed first') and the oracle asserts both orders across the full 0..40 ms sweep and for 0DT in either position, so the mutant is equivalent for every candidate that passes at all.

Line.SetRange("Document No.", DocumentNo) is byte-identical in tasks/starter/CG-AL-X119/CGX119Exporter.Codeunit.al - the reference fix's entire diff is the added Charge case branch plus SetChargeFields - and the spec bounds the work to 'Fix the application so a document's Charge lines export completely.' No fix variant for blank Charge fields deletes the document filter. Optional hardening, not required for B7: add SeedItem + SeedDocLine('DOC2', 20, "CG X119 Line Type"::Item, 'ITM9') to that test and assert Assert.IsFalse(ExportLine.Get('DOC2', 20), 'Rebuilding one document must not create export lines for another document').

ApprovedRecord is a procedure-local record AL blanks at scope entry, and all five fields of the table are assigned before Insert(), so Init() overwrites nothing not then reassigned. No InitValue on any field, and plain Insert() generates a fresh SystemId irrespective of the buffer. Also byte-identical starter code; the fix adds the else-branches that clear the flag.

Pending is a procedure-local record whose only prior operation is a Pending.Get(RecordNo, 'Contact Name') that just returned FALSE, so no row was loaded and the buffer holds at most the searched key - and both of the table's only two fields are then assigned exactly those values before Insert(). No InitValue on 'CG X120 Pending Verification', so Init() is a provable no-op under either interpretation of a failed Get's buffer state.

Identical structure to M0010 in SetCreditLimit: fresh local Pending, guard is a failed Get, both fields of the two-field table assigned to the searched key values before Insert(), no InitValue anywhere on the table.

All four fields of 'CG X121 Contract Line' are reassigned on each of the three loop iterations before Insert(), so the carried-over record is fully overwritten; Init() does not clear filters in AL so the earlier SetRange is unaffected either way, and plain Insert() assigns a new SystemId rather than reusing the buffer's, which is why iteration 2 does not collide. No InitValue and no OnInsert trigger on the table. The codeunit is byte-identical to tasks/starter/CG-AL-X121 - the fix lives in the header table's validation triggers.

< and <= differ only when ChargeableHours = RateCard."Minimum Hours", and the guarded statement there is ChargeableHours := RateCard."Minimum Hours" - an identity self-assignment - so the mutant computes the same Round(ChargeableHours * "Hourly Rate", 0.01) for every input. This is fix-authored code (the starter's HourlyAmountFor was a bare Error), and the oracle does hit the exact boundary: graded case 3 is STANDARD/2 hours against Minimum Hours 2 (expected 180) and case 12 is CALLOUT/4 hours against Minimum Hours 4 (expected 133.33), both identical under either operator.

swap-call-arguments on StrSubstNo(OutOfRangeErr, MinValue, MaxValue) in ValidateInRange. The label is 'Value must be between %1 and %2', so with Min=10/Max=100 the original renders 'Value must be between 10 and 100' and the mutant renders 'Value must be between 100 and 10'. A real observable difference in the ErrorInfo message for every call where MinValue <> MaxValue, and it is in scope: the task YAML requires "Message = 'Value must be between [MinValue] and [MaxValue]' (actual values substituted)". The oracle's two asserterror tests only do Assert.ExpectedError('Value must be between'), a substring that stops short of the substituted values, so the swapped message matches too. A model that emitted the bounds in the wrong order would pass this oracle while producing a nonsensical range message.
mutants.killTest: Add TestValidateInRange_ErrorTextNamesBoundsInOrder: MinValue := 10; MaxValue := 100; asserterror ValidationEngine.ValidateInRange(5, MinValue, MaxValue, 'Amount'); Assert.ExpectedError(StrSubstNo('Value must be between %1 and %2', MinValue, MaxValue)). Building the expected text with StrSubstNo over the same Decimal locals in (min, max) order makes the assertion order-sensitive while matching the implementation's own decimal rendering, so the baseline cannot go red on a Format(Decimal) surprise. The mutant renders '... between 100 and 10', no substring match, test fails.

mutants.justification: Deletes CustTotalQuery.Close(), the last statement of TotalForCustomer. CustTotalQuery is a procedure-local Query variable: opened once, read once, never stored, returned or passed out, and no global or table state is touched. The return value Total was captured from CustTotalQuery.Total_Amount BEFORE the Close() and is neither read nor written afterwards, so the returned Decimal is identical either way. Close() on a Query writes nothing observable; it releases the runtime cursor the runtime releases anyway at procedure exit. Because the variable is fresh per invocation there is no cross-call interaction: each of the four oracle tests constructs its own codeunit instance and each call gets a new Query local, so no 'query already open' error can arise. The task YAML's required body steps list declare / SetRange / Open+Read / return 0 on no row and never mention Close, so no spec obligation is dropped.

conditional-boundary flips the guard DaysUsed < 0 to DaysUsed <= 0 in CalculateProratedRefund. The two versions differ on exactly one input, DaysUsed = 0. Original: guard false, so RefundAmount = (TotalAmount / TotalDays) * (TotalDays - 0) = TotalAmount. Mutant: exit(0). For any TotalAmount <> 0 that is a full-amount versus zero-amount divergence, the most business-visible failure this procedure has. The guarded statement is exit(0), not an identity assignment, so this is NOT a boundary-flip-into-identity equivalence. In scope: the YAML specifies only 'If DaysUsed is negative, return 0.' plus the formula, which fully determines DaysUsed = 0 as a full refund. The oracle exercises DaysUsed = 15, 10 and -5 only; zero is never passed, so a model writing <= 0 passes while silently zeroing every same-day cancellation refund.
mutants.killTest: Add TestRefund_ZeroDaysUsed: Result := SubEngine.CalculateProratedRefund(300, 0, "Subscription Plan"::Basic); Assert.AreEqual(300, Result, 'Cancelling before any day is used must refund the whole amount.'). Basic is 30 days total, so (300 / 30) * (30 - 0) = 300 with exact decimal arithmetic and no rounding sensitivity. Baseline returns 300 and passes; the mutant returns 0 and fails.

crossCutting: GUARDED EARLY EXIT that silently passes: tests/al/hard/CG-AL-H031.Test.al:68-69 and tests/al/hard/CG-AL-H003.Test.al:21-22 both make the enclosing test unconditionally green in a company without the demo data they look for. H003 scores 0.143 and this may be its root cause.

30 of 89 survivors are equivalent in two dominant shapes: RecRef.Close() on a scope-disposed local after the result is latched (11 mutants, H022/H031/M025), and redundant Reset()/Init()/SetCurrentKey restatements (12 mutants, overwhelmingly in seeded-from-bench H/M tasks where the submitting model over-defended).
